tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Who this project key belongs to: the email, the workspace, the domain its tools live on, and the prepaid balance. Call it first if you are not sure which workspace you are acting in.

tools.name: list_tools
tools.description: Every tool in the workspace with its state (running/absent), current release, public URL and who can see it. A 'tool' is one small web app Boathouse runs behind the workspace login.

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: One tool in detail: URL, container state, current release, who it is visible to, and the list of people it has been shared with.

tools.name: deploy
tools.description: Deploy a folder as a tool and make it live at https://<tool>.<workspace domain>. Send the whole folder in `files`, which MUST include a top-level Dockerfile whose process listens on $PORT (8080). Creates the tool on the first deploy; afterwards it replaces the running container. If you got these fil

tools.name: pull
tools.description: Fetch the exact source folder a release was built from, so you can edit it and deploy it back. Returns the release number and the files as text (binary files come back base64 encoded). Tool admins only.

tools.name: logs
tools.description: The tool container's recent log lines, newest last. Use this to find out why a tool is failing.

tools.name: releases
tools.description: The last 20 releases of a tool: number, status (live/superseded/failed), when, who and the note. A failed release shows the last line of its build log.

tools.name: rollback
tools.description: Put an earlier release back in service. With no `to`, goes back to the release before the live one. This rolls back the software, never the database.

tools.name: restart
tools.description: Restart the tool's container with its current release and current secrets.

tools.name: share
tools.description: Give one person access to one tool by email, at a tier: viewer (read only; the gateway blocks their writes), editor (may change the data), admin (may change the software, secrets, sharing). If the person is new, Boat House emails a secure invitation when email is configured. Check emailed in the res

tools.name: unshare
tools.description: Take away one person's access to one tool. They keep their workspace account.

tools.name: request_access
tools.description: Ask to be let into a tool in someone else's workspace, at viewer, editor or admin. Its owners get an email with one Allow button; nobody there runs a command. The person is emailed when it is allowed.

tools.name: access_requests
tools.description: Everyone waiting to be let into one of this workspace's tools: request id, email, tier asked for, and their message. Owners and tool admins.

tools.name: allow_request
tools.description: Let a waiting person in at the tier they asked for. Their tool grant is made and they get an email saying what to do next. Owners and tool admins.

tools.name: set_access
tools.description: Set who a tool is open to by default: 'members' means anyone in the workspace (at the given tier), 'listed' means only the people it has been explicitly shared with. Use 'listed' for anything sensitive.

tools.name: secrets_list
tools.description: The names of a tool's secrets (API keys and the like), when each was last set and by whom. Values are never returned.

tools.name: secrets_set
tools.description: Set one secret on a tool. It is injected as an environment variable of that name and the tool is restarted. Names are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. Never echo the value back to the user.

tools.name: secrets_delete
tools.description: Remove one secret from a tool. It disappears on the tool's next restart or deploy.

tools.name: users_list
tools.description: Everyone in the workspace: role (owner, member or guest), name, and whether they have set a password yet.

tools.name: users_add
tools.description: Add a person to the workspace, or change their role. owner = may spend money, buy domains and manage people, and is admin on every tool; member = may see tools open to members and deploy their own; guest = sees only what is explicitly shared with them. Returns a one-time invite link for someone new.

tools.name: users_invite
tools.description: Resend an invitation to someone in the workspace. New accounts confirm their mailbox through the emailed link; established accounts receive a normal sign-in URL. Password recovery is self-service on that page, and only the account holder's mailbox receives a reset link. Check emailed before offering

tools.name: users_remove
tools.description: Remove a person from the workspace. Their sessions, project keys, invites and tool grants stop working immediately. Owners only.

tools.name: domains_list
tools.description: The addresses this workspace answers on: the free <workspace>.boathousecloud.com address, the primary domain, and every custom domain with its DNS state.

tools.name: domain_check
tools.description: Ask the registrar whether a domain is free and what it costs per year. Buys nothing. total_cents is the price the workspace pays (registrar_cents plus Boathouse's margin_cents); show that one.

tools.name: domain_buy
tools.description: Buy a domain through Boathouse's registrar and point it at this box, paid from the workspace's prepaid balance. Without confirm it only returns the quote (cost now, renewal price, your balance) and buys nothing. Owners only.

tools.name: domain_renewals
tools.description: Read domain expiry dates, renewal status, spending limits and billing problems. Owners only.

tools.name: domain_renewal_set
tools.description: Set automatic renewal and a maximum prepaid renewal charge. Quote the change first, then require explicit approval with confirm true. Turning renewal off lets the domain expire. Owners only.

tools.name: domain_attach
tools.description: Bring a domain the workspace already owns elsewhere: Boathouse starts answering on it and returns the DNS records to make at the current DNS host. Optionally point it at one tool at the same time. Owners only.

tools.name: domain_point
tools.description: Make a domain (and its www) open one tool instead of the workspace's tool list. An empty tool clears it. Owners only.

tools.name: domain_primary
tools.description: Make one of the workspace's domains the primary one: the address tool URLs and emails use. Owners only.

tools.name: domain_dns
tools.description: The DNS records the registrar currently holds for a domain Boathouse bought or manages. Changes nothing.

tools.name: domain_repoint
tools.description: Rewrite a Boathouse-managed domain's DNS records to point at this Boathouse again (after a move, or if someone changed them). Owners only.

tools.name: domain_detach
tools.description: Stop serving a domain. The registration itself is untouched and domain_attach brings it back. Owners only.

tools.name: usage
tools.description: Check storage, memory, CPU and the reason an app is paused. Tool admins only.

tools.name: capacity
tools.description: Quote additional app storage. Show the maximum extra monthly price and get owner approval before confirming. No automatic upgrade. Owners only.

tools.name: billing
tools.description: The workspace's money: prepaid balance, whether it is paused, how fast running tools burn credit, how many days are left, whether a card is on file, and the last ledger lines.

tools.name: prices
tools.description: What Boathouse charges, in plain words: one organization plan for up to five lightweight tools, shared limits, storage, and the domain margin.

tools.name: referral
tools.description: This person's referral code and link, the deal in words, and what each referred workspace has earned them so far (10% of usage charges, paid monthly in cash).

tools.name: topup
tools.description: Open secure Stripe checkout to add prepaid hosting credit; the owner completes payment there. Without confirm it only quotes and returns operation_id. Confirm the same cents and operation_id after user approval; reuse the ID on retries. Between $5.00 (500) and $1,000.00 (100000). Owners only.

tools.name: card_link
tools.description: A one-time link where a workspace owner types a card into Stripe. This is the only part of Boathouse that needs a browser. Owners only.

tools.name: delete_tool
tools.description: Delete a tool: its container, its releases and its sharing. By default the tool's database and files are kept. purge true also destroys them forever, and then requires purge_confirm true as well.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_tools, get_tool, share, request_access, allow_request, users_invite · Private data: deploy, pull, rollback, restart, share, secrets_list, secrets_set, secrets_delete, users_list, users_invite, domain_attach, domain_dns, domain_repoint, billing, delete_tool · Public sink: whoami, deploy, share, request_access, access_requests, allow_request · Destructive: secrets_delete, users_invite, users_remove, delete_tool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_tools, get_tool, share, request_access, allow_request, users_invite · Private data: deploy, pull, rollback, restart, share, secrets_list, secrets_set, secrets_delete, users_list, users_invite, domain_attach, domain_dns, domain_repoint, billing, delete_tool · Public sink: whoami, deploy, share, request_access, access_requests, allow_request · Destructive: secrets_delete, users_invite, users_remove, delete_tool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
